title: [CRY-6] Nothing stops relays accepting previous-epoch access signatures, so a removed member keeps
description: Review finding CRY-6: Nothing stops relays accepting previous-epoch access signatures, so a removed member keeps write access (lens CRY). Location: spec/05-messaging.md:205-208, spec/10-relays.md:527. Fix: The retirement rule exists only by implication. 05:205 ("A member removed after the last countersigned epoch can write until then") presumes that relays stop accepting the old key once a later announcement is accepted, but no sentence requires it. 05:206 only requires verification "against the access public key for the envelope's `channelToken` and `epoch`", which an epoch-N envelope on token N still satisfies. Add a normative rule. After accepting a countersigned announcement for epoch N+1 on a chain, a relay MUST reject envelopes for epoch N or earlier on that chain once a fixed grace period has passed. The grace covers in-flight traffic and members still processing the Commit, which 05:23 makes them buffer. State that the grace period is the removed member's residual write window. Choosing the value (for example 60 s) is a parameter, not a design choice. Full text: notes/review/CRY-verified.md and notes/review/CRY.md.
